rows.ARS:
Red blend Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: DICobey
Exhibition name: Tequila Sunrise
rows.Origin: Bred by Colin Dickson (1956-....) (United Kingdom, 1986). Bred by Patrick Dickson (1926-2012) (United Kingdom, before 1986).
rows.Bloom: Yellow, red edges. Mild fragrance. 40 petals. Medium, full (26-40 petals), cupped-to-flat bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Rounded buds.
rows.Habit:
Armed with thorns / prickles. Medium, glossy foliage.

Height: 30" to 31" (75 to 80cm). Width: up to 2' (up to 60cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
rows.Patents:
Australia - Patent No: 321 on 6 Apr 1994
Application No: 1992/026 on 30 Mar 1992 VIEW PBR PATENT
Synonym: Tequila Sunrise. Applicant: Colin Dickson.

This variety arose from controlled pollination of 'Bonfire' by 'Freedom'. It was bred by Colin Dickson, of Dickson Nurseries, Newtownards, Northern Ireland. 'Tequila Sunrise' has been protected by Plant Variety Rights in United Kingdom since 1988. 'Tequila Sunrise' has been sold in United Kingdom since 1989.

Patent expired. New Zealand - Patent No: 763 on 16 Jun 1993
Application No: ROS347 on 17 Oct 1990
Trade Name: Tequilla Sunrise.
rows.Notes:
Fryer's Roses says Tequila Sunrise has flowers that are a striking scarlet and gold. This rose has won numerous International Awards, including the Royal National Rose Society Gold Medal...
